=== influxdb3 create token --help ===
Create a new auth token

Usage: influxdb3 create token [COMMAND]

Commands:
  --admin       Create or regenerate an admin token
  --permission  Create a resource (eg. database) scoped token

Options:
  -h, --help       Print help information
      --help-all   Print more detailed help information
      --help-full  Print autogenerated help information

=== influxdb3 create token --admin --help ===
Create or regenerate an admin token

Usage: influxdb3 create token --admin [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --regenerate          Regenerate the operator token. By default connects to the main server (http://127.0.0.1:8181).
                                            To use the admin token recovery endpoint, specify --host with the recovery endpoint address
      --name <NAME>         Name of the token
      --expiry <EXPIRY>     Expires in `duration`, e.g 10d for 10 days 1y for 1 year
  -H, --host <host>         The host URL of the running InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_HOST_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8181]
      --token <token>       The token for authentication with the InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server to create permissions. This will be the admin token to create tokens with permissions [env: INFLUXDB3_AUTH_TOKEN]
      --tls-ca <tls-ca>     An optional arg to use a custom ca for useful for testing with self signed certs
      --tls-no-verify       Disable TLS certificate verification [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_NO_VERIFY=]
      --format <FORMAT>     Output format for token, supports just json or text [possible values: json, text]
      --offline             Generate token without connecting to server (enterprise feature)
      --output-file <FILE>  File path to save the token (required with --offline)
  -h, --help                Print help information
      --help-all            Print more detailed help information
      --help-full           Print autogenerated help information

=== influxdb3 create token --permission --help ===
Create a resource (eg. database) scoped token

Usage: influxdb3 create token --permission [PERMISSION] --name <NAME>

Options:
      --permission <PERMISSION>      Permissions in `$RESOURCE_TYPE:$RESOURCE_NAMES:$ACTIONS` format eg. `db:*:read,write`, `system:*:read`, etc. `--permission` may be specified multiple times
      --name <NAME>                  Name of the token
      --expiry <EXPIRY>              Expires in `duration`, e.g 10d for 10 days 1y for 1 year
  -H, --host <host>                  The host URL of the running InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_HOST_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8181]
      --token <token>                The token for authentication with the InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server to create permissions. This will be the admin token to create tokens with permissions [env: INFLUXDB3_AUTH_TOKEN]
      --tls-ca <tls-ca>              An optional arg to use a custom ca for useful for testing with self signed certs
      --tls-no-verify                Disable TLS certificate verification [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_NO_VERIFY=]
      --format <FORMAT>              Output format for token, supports just json or text [possible values: json, text]
      --offline                      Generate token without connecting to server (enterprise feature)
      --output-file <FILE>           File path to save the token (required with --offline)
      --create-databases <DB_NAMES>  Databases to create when the server starts Use this when creating tokens for databases that don't exist yet
  -h, --help                         Print help information
      --help-all                     Print more detailed help information
      --help-full                    Print autogenerated help information

=== influxdb3 show tokens --help ===
List tokens

Usage: influxdb3 show tokens [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -H, --host <HOST_URL>            The host URL of the running InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_HOST_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8181]
      --token <AUTH_TOKEN>         The token for authentication with the InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_AUTH_TOKEN]
      --format <FORMAT>            The format in which to output the response [default: pretty] [possible values: pretty, json, jsonl, csv, parquet]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>  Put all output into the specified file
      --tls-ca <CA_CERT>           An optional arg to use a custom ca for useful for testing with self signed certs [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_CA=]
      --tls-no-verify              Disable TLS certificate verification [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_NO_VERIFY=]
  -h, --help                       Print help information
      --help-all                   Print more detailed help information
      --help-full                  Print autogenerated help information

=== influxdb3 delete token --help ===

Options:
  -H, --host <HOST_URL>          The host URL of the running InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_HOST_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8181]
      --token <AUTH_TOKEN>       The token for authentication with the InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_AUTH_TOKEN]
      --token-name <TOKEN_NAME>  The name of the token to be deleted
      --tls-ca <CA_CERT>         An optional arg to use a custom ca for useful for testing with self signed certs [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_CA=]
      --tls-no-verify            Disable TLS certificate verification [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_NO_VERIFY=]
  -h, --help                     Print help information
      --help-all                 Print more detailed help information
      --help-full                Print autogenerated help information

=== influxdb3 create database --help ===
Create a new database

Usage: influxdb3 create database [OPTIONS] <DATABASE_NAME>

Arguments:
  <DATABASE_NAME>  The name of the database to create. Valid database names are alphanumeric with - and _ allowed and starts with a letter or number [env: INFLUXDB3_DATABASE_NAME=]

Options:
  -H, --host <HOST_URL>
          The host URL of the running InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_HOST_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8181]
      --token <AUTH_TOKEN>
          The token for authentication with the InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_AUTH_TOKEN]
      --retention-period <RETENTION_PERIOD>
          The retention period for the database as a human-readable duration, e.g., "30d", "24h"
      --tls-ca <CA_CERT>
          An optional arg to use a custom ca for useful for testing with self signed certs [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_CA=]
      --tls-no-verify
          Disable TLS certificate verification [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_NO_VERIFY=]
  -h, --help
          Print help information
      --help-all
          Print more detailed help information
      --help-full
          Print autogenerated help information

=== influxdb3 show databases --help ===
List databases

Usage: influxdb3 show databases [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -H, --host <HOST_URL>            The host URL of the running InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_HOST_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8181]
      --token <AUTH_TOKEN>         The token for authentication with the InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_AUTH_TOKEN]
      --show-deleted               Include databases that were marked as deleted in the output
      --format <FORMAT>            The format in which to output the response [default: pretty] [possible values: pretty, json, jsonl, csv, parquet]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT_FILE_PATH>  Put all output into the specified file
      --tls-ca <CA_CERT>           An optional arg to use a custom ca for useful for testing with self signed certs [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_CA=]
      --tls-no-verify              Disable TLS certificate verification [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_NO_VERIFY=]
  -h, --help                       Print help information
      --help-all                   Print more detailed help information
      --help-full                  Print autogenerated help information

=== influxdb3 delete database --help ===
Delete a database

Usage: influxdb3 delete database [OPTIONS] <DATABASE_NAME>

Arguments:
  <DATABASE_NAME>  The name of the database to be deleted [env: INFLUXDB3_DATABASE_NAME=]

Options:
  -H, --host <HOST_URL>     The host URL of the running InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_HOST_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8181]
      --token <AUTH_TOKEN>  The token for authentication with the InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_AUTH_TOKEN]
      --hard-delete <WHEN>  When to perform hard deletion (never/now/default/timestamp). Examples: 'never', 'now', 'default', '2024-06-18T10:30:00Z'
      --data-only           Delete only data while keeping the catalog entries along with all associated resources (tokens, triggers, LVC/DVC, processing engine configurations, etc.)
      --remove-tables       When used with `--data-only`, this removes database data and table resources (caches), while preserving database-level resources (tokens, triggers, LVC/DVC, processing engine configurations, etc.)
      --tls-ca <CA_CERT>    An optional arg to use a custom ca for useful for testing with self signed certs [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_CA=]
      --tls-no-verify       Disable TLS certificate verification [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_NO_VERIFY=]
  -h, --help                Print help information
      --help-all            Print more detailed help information
      --help-full           Print autogenerated help information

Examples:
  # Remove all data, tables, and linked resources (caches, triggers, tokens)
  influxdb3 delete database my_db

  # Remove all data, keep all resources and table schemas
  influxdb3 delete database my_db --data-only

  # Remove all data and tables, keep database-level resources
  influxdb3 delete database my_db --data-only --remove-tables

=== influxdb3 update database --help ===
Update a database

Usage: influxdb3 update database [OPTIONS] --database <DATABASE_NAME>

Options:
  -H, --host <HOST_URL>
          The host URL of the running InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_HOST_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8181]
  -d, --database <DATABASE_NAME>
          The name of the database to operate on [env: INFLUXDB3_DATABASE_NAME=]
      --token <AUTH_TOKEN>
          The token for authentication with the InfluxDB 3 Enterprise server [env: INFLUXDB3_AUTH_TOKEN]
  -r, --retention-period <RETENTION_PERIOD>
          The retention period as a human-readable duration (e.g., "30d", "24h") or "none" to clear
      --tls-ca <CA_CERT>
          An optional arg to use a custom ca for useful for testing with self signed certs [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_CA=]
      --tls-no-verify
          Disable TLS certificate verification [env: INFLUXDB3_TLS_NO_VERIFY=]
  -h, --help
          Print help information
      --help-all
          Print more detailed help information
      --help-full
          Print autogenerated help information
